actions.body: Research into computational creativity highlights that autonomous problem formulation—the process by which an agent defines its own questions—is distinct from routine knowledge manipulation. Current theoretical models, supported by active inference frameworks, suggest that agents construct objectives by evaluating the 'interestingness' or 'value' of potential problem spaces against internal policy models. This process mirrors human creative cognition, where imagination is constrained by existing skill and intellect. [source-1809dbae217646a5] [source-c70adfa002384610]. Moving beyond theoretical definitions, the integration of these processes into practice requires robust evaluation mechanisms. Agents must distinguish between arbitrary novelty and meaningful progress. [source-6ee93795fbf2497c]. Summary: Computational creativity depends on structured problem formulation and iterative evaluation; autonomous agents identify novel, worthwhile problems by resolving the conflict between their internal policy models and the potential information value of new inquiries.
actions.lede: How do we define the boundary between assigned tasks and autonomous inquiry in intelligent systems?
